confounds: The AdaLoRA arm and the uniform arm share one block configuration: the archived rank_pattern puts rank 4 on all 324 modules with the same per-block parameter counts ({"llm_deep": 1318912, "llm_mid": 2308096, "llm_shallow": 989184, "vision": 2621440}), so 'AdaLoRA' and 'uniform allocation' are the same rank plan and the comparison against the Gamma plan varies method and configuration at once.
Every archived cell on this plane shares one pre-training energy, E0 = [23470.845703125], so both arms see the same reference data and the same evaluation samples.
AdaLoRA's trainable-parameter count is not exactly the budget (measured 7238928 against 7237632, 0.0179% high), so the arms are matched only under the cost model.

The two scripts do not start from the same first-epoch loss at seed 42 (AdaLoRA 1.5595 against Gamma 1.5455 at lr 5e-5), so the CE-loss axes are not matched across scripts and no matched-loss claim is made here.

what_may_be_claimed_about_adalora: In every archived cell where AdaLoRA and the Gamma-guided rule share budget, learning rate and seed (4 cells), AdaLoRA reaches the lower alignment energy: the per-cell difference runs [-3416.5625, -2789.873047, -4059.398438, -4242.140625], mean -3627.0, 95% t CI [-4678.51181, -2575.475495].

The direction is consistent but the archived comparison is under-powered: with 4 matched cells the exact two-sided sign test bottoms out at p=0.125, so the AdaLoRA advantage is reported as a consistent direction, not as a significant one.

The Gamma-guided rule does beat the published non-adaptive allocation rules at the shared base-rank-1 arm: its arm is 196.5 against [["ShapLoRA-style (our block-level reimplementation)", 444.0], ["IGU-LoRA-style (our block-level reimplementation)", 333.0], ["HALoRA-style (our block-level reimplementation)", 284.0], ["NTK-diagonal rule (CLIP-derived, our arm)", 396.0], ["official IGU-LoRA code, name-proxy adapter", 240.5]].
what_may_be_claimed_about_rc: Within the LLaVA-1.5-7B blank-image protocol at the archived operating point, the sign of dE changes between r=5 and r=6; the ten-seed fit puts the crossing at 5.334 (95% bootstrap CI [5.195417, 5.467364]), bracketed by those two ranks and not localised to one.
The sign split at the bracket is complete in that stratum: {"all_runs_at_r5_negative": true, "all_runs_at_r6_positive": true, "r5": {"mean": -43.7, "n": 10}, "r6": {"mean": 87.3, "n": 10}}.
The re-run family (five seeds, current script defaults) places the crossing at 5.260, inside the same bracket.

Outside that protocol the crossing moves: llava_blank3ep_cloud10 -> 5.333588, llava_e2_extra -> 5.252, llava_e2_sweep -> 14.200631, llava_ers_1epoch -> 46.759029, llava_rerun5 -> 5.259887, llava_samplesize_windows -> 5.549195, llava_seed5_aggregate -> 5.259887, llava_sharegpt -> 4.957447
what_may_not_be_claimed_about_adalora: The comparison is confounded: the AdaLoRA arm runs the uniform rank-4 plan on all 324 modules, the same rank plan as the plain uniform control, so it does not isolate adaptive rank allocation from block configuration.

It does not reverse on the energy axis at any archived learning rate or seed, but it does reverse in the neighbouring comparison: plain uniform rank beats the Gamma rule in 3 archived cells ([[0.0003, 42], [0.0003, 123], [0.001, 123]]).
No matched-loss claim is available: the two scripts do not start from the same first-epoch loss, so the loss ordering between them is not comparable.
The AdaLoRA arm is not exactly on budget under measurement (0.0179% above the cost model), so budget matching holds only in the cost model.
what_may_not_be_claimed_about_rc: r_c is not a single number across backbones. Of the 5 families, 3 contain at least one stratum with a sign crossing (["llava-1.5-7b", "qwen2-vl-2b", "smolvlm-500m"]), 2 contain none anywhere in their measured rank range (["clip-vit-base-patch32", "qwen2-vl-7b"]), and only 1 yields one well-defined crossing (["smolvlm-500m"]). LLaVA-1.5-7B is the one family in which a crossing can be bracketed under a named protocol, and even there the stratum spread runs from 4.96 to 46.76, so no single r_c holds inside the family.

Qwen2-VL-2B: in the training-energy field the sign of dE is set by the image condition, not by the rank - every rank r=1..16 is positive with real images and negative with blank ones, so no crossing exists there. The held-out energy field does contain one crossing, at 5.897, but it sits in a single bracket [5, 6] whose bootstrap CI [3.618517, 6.477364] spans more than a rank, so it does not localise r_c either.

The CLIP ViT-B/32 retrieval arm never crosses in any of its four strata: the sign of its energy change is set by the training window and by which energy is read (training energy positive at 16 pairs and negative at 1024; held-out energy negative at both), never by the rank, so it cannot corroborate any rank threshold.

The curvature observable on the same LLaVA backbone does not corroborate a rank threshold either: on the primary seed line the second-order share is negative at every archived rank in [5, 6, 8, 12, 16, 24, 64] and rises monotonically toward zero without crossing it (monotone rising toward zero: true), and the manuscript's own claim table already records that the sign is not stable across seeds at this step.

r_c is not even stable inside LLaVA: the five-seed stratum means at r=5 are not a cross-environment constant (stack means {"torch 2.12/cu130": -43.7, "torch 2.4/cu121": 25.25, "torch 2.9/cu130": -23.0}; software-stack share of the r=5 variance 0.45, 95% CI [0.21198180448528658, 0.7471951281145658]).
